title: Born on a Wednesday.
caption: February 26, 1992, Lagos. A middle child: small, quick, creative, and already everywhere at once.

title: Started school at four.
caption: Left primary school with two titles: neatest boy and health prefect. One of them still holds.

title: Nine years old, sent to boarding school.
caption: Federal Government College, Oyo State: three years as the smallest boy in a rural school, bullied for speaking English and for being scattered. Bright, creative, drifting in and out of class. The scatter wouldn't get its name for decades.

title: Two more schools before the finish line.
caption: A year at Livingstone Model College, then Lagos State Model College Igbonla. Wanted to draw buildings for a living; landed in arts class studying to be a lawyer. Graduated at fifteen.

title: University of Lagos, round one.
caption: Applied for Law at sixteen, got Political Science. Spent more of it as Rhymesmith, trading bars in campus rap battles with guys who became household names. The degree didn't happen; the stage presence stayed.

title: Punch at parties, a voice on air.
caption: Mixed and sold party punch to stay afloat, met Tosin and Nas, friends to this day, and talked my way onto radio for the first time.

title: Radio, properly.
caption: Trained at the Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria; an internship at Eko FM became a full-time presenter's seat, and a sports show ended up syndicated on Rhythm FM. Six years of learning to hold a room with nothing but a voice.

title: Youngest project manager in the building.
caption: Three years at West Midland Communications, setting up computer-based testing centres for the national university entrance exam. First taste of shipping something real at scale.

title: Back to UNILAG, this time for my mother.
caption: Mass Communication, done right: class governor, departmental and faculty debate champion, university debate team. People had written me off; she never did.

title: Jumia, where product found me.
caption: Joined customer experience at what became Africa's biggest e-commerce company, moved to the product experience team, and left in 2017 to finish the degree. The love for product never left.

title: Graduated into a recession with a Mass Communication degree.
caption: University of Lagos, top 3% of the class. That training still helps me explain a product decision and defend it in a room.

title: Became someone's first-ever product hire.
caption: No playbook, three mobile apps, and 29 Nigerian states I actually travelled to so I'd know who I was building for.

title: Founding consultant at Agramondis.
caption: Seconded from Farm Crowdy to build a sister company's presence from nothing — brand, website, research papers. Turns out the writing habit was a career skill.

title: MasterCard Foundation Scholar.
caption: A post-grad in Technology, Design & Entrepreneurship. It gave a formal name to work I had already been doing.

title: Joined Paystack, learned how money actually moves.
caption: A Stripe company. Took a payment idea from a single line to tens of millions in volume, and learned that I enjoy the operational detail behind a payment that actually clears.

title: Married her — on our shared birthday.
caption: We met at Farm Crowdy in 2019; she sat one seat and one level away. Born the same day, February 26, 1992 — we turned thirty and got married on the same morning.

title: A friend put a racquet in my hand.
caption: Abby from Paystack introduced us to tennis. My wife and I have been chasing a clean backhand together ever since.

title: Ran corporate banking across two continents and five PMs.
caption: Nigeria, the UK, and a lot of 6am calls. Grew the team; one mentee ended up running a whole division.

title: Moved to Toronto. Marqeta. Still here.
caption: Landed in Calgary in March, Toronto by November. Lead PM on a card-issuing platform that moves billions. I kept building prototypes myself because that is still how I understand a product.

title: Toronto. Married. Still chasing a clean backhand.
caption: Writing essays for minds that think in spirals, making a little art, and losing to better players on weekends.
